newsitem.title: PERU: Lima shares end up led by industrial sector gains.
newsitem.headline: Lima shares end up led by industrial sector gains.

text.p: Shares on the Lima stock exchange closed up Thursday for the second successive day as industrial companies showed solid gains, brokers said.
They added Friday's trade was expected to show the same trend.

Thursday, the General Index .IGRA rose 1.76 percent to 1,475.7 points, while the blue-chip Selective Index .ISEL climbed 1.48 percent to 2,035.2 points, according to preliminary stock figures. Volume was a healthy 53.6 million soles ($21.6 million), where 61 stocks rose, 13 fell and 28 were stable in a total of 2,671 operations.
"The day's rise propelled by specific news in certain companies," said Vanesa Chiesa of local brokerage Cruz Blanca.
Brewery Backus y Johnston rose 1.89 percent to 2.69 soles, accounting for six percent of total volume, on rumors that the company plans to fuse its subsidiaries, brokers said.
In a good day for the breweries, Compania Nacional de Cerveza also rose, closing up 4.19 percent to 1.00 sol on 1.4 million shares.

Buenaventura also saw active trade rising 1.19 percent to 21.25 soles after Wednesday's news that the polymetal miner had won a lawsuit to exercise preemptive rights on shares in Peru's largest gold project Yanacocha, brokers said.
D'Onofrio DON.LM soared 10.19 percent to 1.19 soles on continued rumors of a takeover bid by a foreign company despite strong denials by the chocolate producer.
"The market is taking it for granted that it has already been sold to Nestle," said Alberto Liu of local brokerage Peruval.
